object_description: compact five-storey school on the corner with a kindergarten pavilion over a large single-storey plinth
design_condition: two buildings of different size delimit the large base area across the diagonal, the compact school taking the corner and the kindergarten pavilion relating in scale to the small-scale development along the side street

positive: The orthogonal setting of two buildings of different size responds appropriately to the heterogeneous neighbourhood
The compact five-storey school occupies the corner and delimits the green caesura with the planned high-rise
The kindergarten is cleverly integrated as a pavilion relating in scale to the small-scale development
The urban figure creates a spacious, zoned courtyard area
Covered roofs create an interesting connection between the two streets
School and kindergarten are clearly and simply organised
Two class clusters per floor enclose the common inner access area ending in a spacious two-flight staircase
All public uses are in the base building and can each be operated independently
A deep courtyard guarantees natural lighting for the music school
The double gymnasium is optimally organised operationally and can be used independently of the school
negative: The new urban ensemble remains rather imprecise and very self-referential in the transition to the neighbourhood
The large single-storey plinth is seen as a less urban response
Neither a contrast nor a dialogue with the adjacent park is sought
The ground floor along the street takes the form of a closed concrete wall towards the park
The open space concept remains rather vague overall
The concept refers strongly to the inner world of the complex without emphasising its qualities
The inner access area is very introverted with no connection to the outside
There is a lack of innovation on a pedagogical level in the floor plan typology
The placement and dimensions of the deep courtyard appear random and add little spatial quality
